Club history · 2011 – 2020

One club,
seven names

From a public linebattle group in April 2011 to Coldstream Gaming today — the same people, renamed again and again. 315 people passed through; 94 followed the community through at least one rebrand; 627 events were called.

Where it starts

The oldest surviving thing in the lineage is the Official21stPA YouTube channel, opened 3 April 2011 — two days before the 21stPA Public Linebattle Group appeared on Steam. Nine weeks later that group was wound up in one line: “21stPA Is now disbanded, take the tags off please, Thanks.”

The est. 2011 on the badge holds up. Midnight Mercenarys was founded 28 June 2011, and the Nox Viator group still describes the community in its own words as “a PC Gaming Community founded June 28, 2011.” Three separate records, one year.

The community has not always told the same story about the month, though. RoaR Gaming's description claims “a PC Gaming Community founded December, 2011” — six months later than Nox Viator says. The Steam group founding dates favour the earlier claim: the 21stPA group existed in April 2011 and Midnight Mercenarys in June.

The films, and what they were

Ten recordings that document a specific moment, with what the written records say was happening around them. Press play to load the video.

2011 · 21st Pennsylvania

The oldest thing that survives

21st Regiment of Pennsylvania Tribute · 420 views

The Official21stPA channel opened on 3 April 2011 — two days before the 21stPA Public Linebattle Group was founded on Steam. Nothing older exists in the lineage. Nine weeks later the group was wound up with a one-line notice: “21stPA Is now disbanded, take the tags off please, Thanks.”

Watch on YouTube →

2012 · the migration

The last Mount & Musket linebattle

Last MM LB event - 2nd Coldstream Regiment of Footguards (Part 1) · 105 views

Filmed as the unit left Mount & Musket for Napoleonic Wars. Mount & Musket is still named in 15 announcements during 2012 and 6 more in 2013, so the old mod did not die overnight — but this is the farewell to it, and the point the Coldstream name takes over.

Watch on YouTube →

2012 · identity

The recruitment film

To be a 2nd Coldstream Footguard · 370 views

The regiment selling itself. This is the era when the FSE forum thread was titled “Recruiting NA Players” and the first fourteen recruits were welcomed in a single post on 19 November 2012.

Watch on YouTube →

2012 · competitive

League debut — 2ndCS vs 3eVolt

RWL Week 1 | 2ndCS vs 3eVolt · 426 views

Week one of a Regimental Warfare League season. Beyond the public linebattles, the regiment fielded a competitive side against other named units — the closest thing the community had to a fixture list.

Watch on YouTube →

2012 · head to head

Against the 8th Regiment of Foot, 20 October 2012

2nd Coldstream Guards vs. 8th Regiment of Foot 10/20/2012 · 740 views

One of the few videos carrying its own date. It sits three weeks before the FSE recruitment thread opened on 12 November 2012 — proof the regiment was already running events well before it advertised on the forum.

Watch on YouTube →

2012 · siege night

Tuesday siege night, 22 May 2012

Tuesday Siege Event 5-22 Part 1 · 148 views

Part of a recurring siege series. The Steam announcements from that same week are pure artillery: “Artillery Training at 8 Est. TONIGHT DON’T FORGET!”, then “ARTY TRAINING NOW FALL INTO SERVER!”, and best of all — “Want to get shot at by a cannon? Get on teamspeak, We need you!”

Watch on YouTube →

2012 · peak

The most-watched thing the club ever made

Napoleonic Wars - 2nd Coldstream's Friday LB Highlights · 1.1K views

At 1.1K views this is the high-water mark of the channel — more than double any other upload. It comes from the busiest stretch in the community’s history: 324 event calls went out in 2012 alone.

Watch on YouTube →

2012 · cross-referenced

The December linebattles, filmed and announced

Napoleonic Wars - December 6th/7th Linebattles with the 2ndCS · 181 views

This one can be matched to the paperwork. On 7 December 2012 the forum thread carried “Linebattle tomorrow @ 7PM Central / 8PM Eastern”, while the Steam group was calling members in with “Fall into teamspeak lads, training before the linebattle starting soon!”

Watch on YouTube →

2012 · the people

Player spotlight — Gooner

Coldstream Player Spotlight - Gooner · 645 views

The club making a film about one of its own members rather than about a battle. At 645 views it outperformed nearly every linebattle recording, which says something about what the community was actually for.

Watch on YouTube →

2020 · the revival

Back again, eight years later

2nd Coldstream Guards - Official Public Linebattle 7/16/20 · 25 views

The 2020 revival under the 2nd Coldstream Guard group, which ran 18 events between April and July. The language had changed with the platform: “fall into teamspeak” became “We’re starting boys, hop into discord!”

Watch on YouTube →

The seven eras

Every Steam group in the order it was founded. Colour marks the brand family — Coldstream in scarlet, Midnight Mercs in indigo, Nox Viator in violet, the 21st in Union blue.

“Fall into teamspeak”

How the club called people in — and how that changed. TeamSpeak appears in 567 announcements between 2011 and 2016; Discord takes over from 2016.

“Everyone fall into teamspeak, regimental training starting!” — 30 Dec 2012
“Want to get shot at by a cannon? Get on teamspeak, We need you!” — 28 May 2012
“Forget it, I'm beyond pissed. We'll talk about this attendance.” — 27 May 2012
“We're starting boys, hop into discord!” — 28 Jun 2020

The phrase “fall in” was used 203 times. It is the closest thing the community has to a catchphrase, and it disappears exactly when TeamSpeak does.

The Napoleonic regiment, in detail

The 2012–2016 era left the deepest paper trail: 885 posts over 59 pages of the FSE forum.

Forum posts per month, Nov 2012 – Mar 2016. Pale marks are silent months.

It renamed itself twelve times

Each forum reply stores the thread title as it stood, so the thread carries its own renaming history.

#FromTitle
01 November 12, 2012 2nd Coldstream Regiment of Footguards [Recruiting NA Players]
02 September 21, 2014 2nd Coldstream Regiment of Footguards [Recruiting Mature NA Players]
03 September 22, 2014 2nd Coldstream Regiment of Footguards [Recruiting Mature NA & EU Players]

Standing orders

  1. Never teamkill; if it was an accident, apologise at once.
  2. When permission to speak is in effect, ask before speaking.
  3. Never type while in line, at training, or in a linebattle — it slows everyone down.
  4. Try your best and follow orders. Running from battle or a command is punished.
  5. Always work as a team. If you decide you do not need teamwork, leave the regiment.
  6. Do not retaliate against teamkillers; report them to an admin.

The rank ladder

The regiment drew its own insignia — twelve ranks from Recruit to Lieutenant Colonel. These images were hosted on Photobucket and have survived thirteen years; they are embedded here so they cannot be lost again.

Sources, and what is missing

Seven Steam groups (membership, founding dates and all 1,210 announcements), the FSE forum thread (885 posts over 59 pages), and two YouTube channels. Everything fetched once, cached, analysed offline.

Known gaps. Steam does not publish when a member joined a group, so era rosters show who is in the group now, not who was there then — the dated intakes are the only true point-in-time roster. Private profiles do not appear at all, which is why named rosters run short of member counts. RoaR Gaming (from October 2017) is unscraped. The TaleWorlds thread sits behind a bot challenge and was left alone.

Event counts are announcements calling an event, not attendance records. They measure how busy an era was, not how many turned up.

Compiled 19 August 2026 from public Steam, FSE forum and YouTube records. Built for River.
